summary.headline: NRB Bearings Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19.2% to INR370 crore and PAT 15% to INR38 crore; management guides to a long-term INR2,700-3,000 crore FY31 vision.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations rose to INR370 crore from INR310 crore (19.2% YoY) and PAT rose to INR38 crore from INR33 crore (15%). Standalone sales grew 14.7% YoY, standalone PAT 31.7% and standalone EBITDA 21.7%. Management focused on diversification into aerospace (via the Mahant Tool Room/MTR acquisition), electrification, off-highway and robotics, plus a first US Corvette planet-pin production order. Management declined to give quarterly or FY27 growth guidance and repeatedly redirected questions to the trailing 12-month baseline.

financial_highlights.change: Up from INR800 crore in prior call, after adding US Corvette win

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Now 14% of total revenue, up from 11%, with 34% growth; management tracks this annually, not quarterly.

segments.name: Aerospace / defense (MTR / Mahant Tool Room)
segments.commentary: Acquisition closed about one month before the call. Current MTR order book about INR30 crore; FY31 target INR300 crore revenue with INR90 crore profit contribution. Management did not give a FY27 revenue figure.

segments.name: Regular (non-aerospace) defense
segments.commentary: Order book about INR20 crore; combined defense order book about INR50 crore per management.

segments.name: Heavy mobility / off-highway
segments.commentary: Accredited US defense supplier for heavy vehicle applications; supplies French and US defense via Meritor; JCB UK acquired as customer.

guidance_outlook: FY31 vision: management says trailing 12-month growth of 14.28% extrapolates to about INR2,700 crore; INR3,000 crore is the aspirational level. Guidance corrected to this basis, from the earlier INR2,500 crore.
Management declined to commit to FY27 growth (analyst asked about 15-20%) and said it prefers annual, not quarterly, guidance.
EBITDA/PAT margin framed as 18-20% on an annual basis; quarterly variation expected due to cost lags.

Unitec JV (industrial cylindrical roller bearings for large gearboxes): INR110 crore investment, INR130 crore capacity, commissioning by April 2027; location moved from Hyderabad to Aurangabad (Shendra), with partly ready facility purchased.
Capex programme totals INR270 crore: INR60 crore spent, a further INR100 crore ordered or in process; management said INR100 crore capex supports about INR130 crore sales.
Management expects MTR order book to convert into revenue in FY27 but would not quantify.
risks_watch: Guidance credibility: management gave no FY27 number and reframed the FY31 target repeatedly; numbers were corrected mid-call (INR800 crore nomination referred to USD terms in one answer).
Input-cost pressure from power, logistics and petroleum products; pass-through through price increases is not yet quantified.
Aerospace execution: MTR revenue timing is hard to predict per management; order book only about INR30 crore.
Unitec JV commissioning by April 2027 and capacity ramp, given the site change.
Data centre and robotics products are pre-revenue; no timelines given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategy and growth narrative, but deliberately evasive on near-term numbers: repeatedly declined FY27 and quarterly guidance and shifted questions to trailing 12-month averages.
key_quotes: So it's more a question of not whether it's going to be INR20 crores this year, but whether this year's INR20 crores will become INR100 crores next year.
Our industrial business is 14% of our total now. It's grown steadily from 11% to 14%.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth continue at the 19% seen in Q1, and will FY31 guidance move from INR2,500 crore to INR3,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY27 guidance and said the trailing 12-month growth of 14.38% would reach about INR2,730 crore by FY31; it said INR2,500 crore was too low and the guidance was being corrected to the trailing basis (later stated as 14.28%).

qa_highlights.question: Will the Unitec JV be commissioned by year-end, and is the INR110 crore fully spent there?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is targeted for April 2027. INR110 crore is the investment, and capacity is INR130 crore; the location moved from Hyderabad to Aurangabad, where a partly ready facility has been bought.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is industrial, and how fast can it reach 20-25%? Do EV programmes carry higher bearing content per vehicle?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial is 14% of revenue, up from 11%, with 34% growth, tracked annually. Management said NRB is EV-agnostic, with about 70% of its applications common across EV, ICE and hybrid, and did not quantify per-vehicle content.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence order book, RFQ pipeline and FY27/FY31 revenue expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: MTR order book about INR30 crore (MTR closed about a month earlier); FY31 target INR300 crore revenue and INR90 crore profit. NRB is an accredited US heavy-vehicle defence supplier and supplies French and US defence through Meritor. No FY27 figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses jump about INR10 crore this quarter, and what is being done about it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to electricity, logistics and petroleum-linked cost escalation, offset by VAVE (value engineering and cost reduction) and price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return above 20% over the long term, and is the Mahant Tool Room core team retained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 18-20% margin on an annual basis, with quarterly variation. On the team, it said Mr. Mallappa now leads the aerospace defence segment and the core team has been retained.

capex_capacity: Total capex programme INR270 crore: about INR60 crore already spent, a further about INR100 crore already ordered or in process; management said INR100 crore of capex supports about INR130 crore of sales.

Unitec JV: investment INR110 crore, capacity to cover about INR130 crore; commissioning targeted by April 2027. Location moved from Hyderabad to Aurangabad (Shendra region) on logistics and cost considerations; a partly ready facility and land already purchased to cut lead time.
Management said the INR110 crore figure is investment, not turnover, after an analyst's question framed it as capex.

MTR (Mahant Tool Room) capacity: management said manpower is a small part of aerospace capability; the key constraints are equipment, infrastructure, space quality and supply chain, with NRB as a supplier to MTR.

Data centre bearings are in product development, with no launch timeline given; robotics and humanoid products are being developed as customised precision components and bearings, with no volumes disclosed.
demand_pricing: Trailing 12-month revenue growth cited as 14.38% in one answer and 14.28% in another; management used this as the baseline for the INR2,700 crore FY31 extrapolation.
Industrial business is 14% of total revenue (up from 11%), with 34% growth; tracked annually, not quarterly.
Lifetime nominated business raised to INR1,100 crore from INR800 crore, with the US Corvette planet-pin win (about 300,000 peak volume) added.
Defence order book about INR50 crore in total: MTR about INR30 crore (including spherical bearing orders) and NRB regular defence about INR20 crore.
MTR FY31 target: INR300 crore revenue and INR90 crore profit contribution; no FY27 figure given. Management said FY27 conversion of order book is expected but hard to predict.

Cost pressure: other expenses rose about INR10 crore QoQ on electricity, logistics and petroleum-linked costs; management said the offset is VAVE (value engineering and cost reduction) plus price increases.

Margin framing: 18-20% on an annual basis, with quarterly variation from cost lags. EV strategy: about 70% of applications are EV, ICE and hybrid agnostic (chassis, transmissions, steering); BMW i steering launch in 2027.

Total capex programme INR270 crore (INR60 crore spent, ~INR100 crore ordered or in process), supporting ~INR130 crore of sales

growth.why: Consolidated revenue rose 19.2% YoY to INR370 crore and the trailing 12-month growth is about 14.3%, with a INR270 crore capex programme and Unitec JV commissioning by April 2027; however management gave no FY27 growth guidance and the FY31 INR2,700-3,000 crore figure is aspirational, so the outlook is moderately positive rather than firmly backed.
